says: Three isolated runtimes of the installed candidate, each starting from a fresh profile that access.profile.read shows active at generation 1. On the laptop, Alice binds her device key, registers a personal notes source and locks the profile (generation 2). An unlock while the private key sits beside the public one is refused private_key_beside_public, and one through the login agent is refused agent_not_owned_here; both write nothing and leave the profile locked. With the key laid out as the unlock binding states and the agent this runtime owns, the unlock at a terminal is recorded active at generation 2 with key_mode real. Her next commit of the notes source lands on a volume whose encryption the installation did not observe: it commits and discloses storage_not_encrypted beside the commit rather than claiming a protection nobody observed. On a bare system with no agent the runtime can start and own, the locked profile's unlock is refused keystore_missing with no recovery: nothing is written, no plaintext or mocked key stands in, and a later profile read still shows it locked at generation 2. In the test harness, the unlock opens the profile with a fixture key the harness supplied: the owner records it active with key_mode fixture, naming the fixture's digest, never real. When the harness then submits its own access state claiming its key ran for real, it is refused as runtime-owned: a mocked key certifies no production assurance, and no caller can hand the owner a state saying otherwise (a stored state recording a fixture key as real is not a record the schema admits).
